paper_metadata.title: Research on the Design of Financial Data Analysis Platform with Joint PSO-HQCNN and RPA Robot Visualization Technology

summary: The paper proposes an HQCNN-based RPA financial data analysis workflow and reports that HQCNN reduces loss by 0.0056, raising training accuracy to 98.28% and test accuracy to 96.81% versus CNN. With PSO-HQCNN, recognition accuracy reaches 96.85%, but training time increases to 23.6 hours, compared with 1 hour for HQCNN and 1.2 hours for CNN; no hardware, qubit count, or circuit depth is reported.

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical convolutional neural network (HQCNN) for financial data analysis/RPA visualization, compared against a classical CNN baseline.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: 100 iterations in reported comparison; stability noted after 90 iterations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical image/data are compressed to 8x2 size and mapped from values in [0,1] to [0,π/2] for quantum-state preparation
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize loss for CAPTCHA/financial-system image recognition and validation in an RPA workflow

problem_instance.description: Recognition/validation of financial-system CAPTCHA-like images for automated identification in an RPA financial data analysis platform

dataset_specification.description: CAPTCHA image containing 4 characters; images are segmented before training

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Images are segmented using pixel projection with threshold 13; images with extremely incomplete segmentation are manually removed; images are compressed to 8x2; classical values in [0,1] are mapped to [0,π/2] for quantum-state encoding
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Repeated experiments over 100 iterations; compared loss, training accuracy, and test accuracy against CNN

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Pixel-projection segmentation; manual removal of badly segmented samples; image compression and normalization to [0,1] before angle mapping
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Visualization/report generation via RPA, including moving charts from Excel to Word templates

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: loss decreases and becomes stable after about 90 iterations; less fluctuation after 60 iterations

speedup_claims.conditions: Compared on 100 iterations for financial-system CAPTCHA recognition in an RPA workflow
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper reports improved accuracy and lower loss, but no asymptotic or wall-clock speedup claim for HQCNN over CNN.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not assessable from the paper; no qubit count, circuit depth, or hardware platform is reported.
limiting_factors: No qubit count or circuit depth reported
Only a small image-recognition benchmark is shown
Improvement is modest and compared only against a classical CNN

notes: The paper reports HQCNN architecture details (1 quantum layer, 2x2 core size) but does not explicitly state total qubit count, circuit depth, simulator/QPU, gate counts, or optimizer details; these are left null.
speedup_order is inferred as none_proven because the paper reports improved accuracy and training time trade-offs, not an asymptotic quantum speedup.
The paper reports HQCNN improves training accuracy by 0.93 percentage points and test accuracy by 0.36 percentage points over CNN, with loss reduced by 0.0056.
This is a small benchmark improvement, not a demonstrated practical quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Particle-swarm-optimized HQCNN (PSO-HQCNN) for financial-system image recognition/validation, compared against CNN and HQCNN baselines.

algorithm.variant: PSO-HQCNN (particle swarm optimization combined with HQCNN)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: reported recognition/validation comparison; no explicit stopping criterion beyond training completion
algorithm.parameter_initialization: PSO-based joint optimization of classical-to-quantum parameters; exact initialization not specified

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical CAPTCHA images are compressed to 8x2 and mapped from [0,1] to [0,π/2] before quantum-state preparation
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize recognition accuracy for financial-system image identification in an RPA workflow

problem_instance.description: Recognition/validation of segmented financial-system CAPTCHA images for automated identification

dataset_specification.description: CAPTCHA image containing 4 characters; segmentation performed before training

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Pixel-projection segmentation with threshold 13; isometric cutting when image width > 30; manual removal of incomplete segments; compression to 8x2; mapping to quantum-state data
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison of recognition accuracy and training time among CNN, HQCNN, and PSO-HQCNN; automatic identification system executed 200 times with success rate reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Same segmentation and encoding pipeline as HQCNN experiment
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: RPA visualization/report generation and automatic identification workflow

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: PSO-HQCNN loss slightly lower and less fluctuating than HQCNN/CNN; recognition accuracy highest

speedup_claims.conditions: Recognition/validation comparison for segmented financial-system CAPTCHA images
speedup_claims.caveats: PSO-HQCNN improves recognition accuracy but has the longest training time; no quantum computational speedup is claimed.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not assessable from the paper; no qubit count, circuit depth, or hardware platform is reported.
limiting_factors: No qubit count or circuit depth reported
PSO-HQCNN improves recognition accuracy but at much higher training time
No asymptotic or practical quantum speedup is demonstrated

notes: The paper reports PSO-HQCNN as a hybrid optimization of HQCNN but does not specify qubit count, hardware, simulator, gate counts, or circuit depth beyond the architecture table; these remain null.
The reported 23.6-hour training time is for PSO-HQCNN, but the paper does not separate quantum vs classical runtime components.
PSO-HQCNN achieves the best recognition accuracy at 96.85%, compared with 96.20% for HQCNN and 95.65% for CNN.
However, the training time is 23.6 hours, far longer than HQCNN (1 hour) and CNN (1.2 hours), so no practical advantage is shown.
